text.p: Backers of a C$300 million Alberta pipeline proposal that would end NOVA Corp's monopoly on natural gas transport in the province said on Wednesday that the line's design was complete and final agreements were sent to shippers.
PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd and Westcoast Energy Inc said they expected to file their application for the Palliser pipeline with Canada's National Energy Board by November 15.
The pipeline, which would include about 250 km of mainline and 700 km of gathering lines, would run to southwestern Saskatchewan from just east of Calgary.
The new design includes twice as much gathering pipeline than originally planned, the companies said.

PanCanadian, which produces most of its gas in southern Alberta, devised the Palliser proposal because it was paying the same amount to transport production to the Alberta-Saskatchewan border as producers in the uppermost regions of the province.
All NOVA shippers pay the same amount to ship gas in Alberta under a decades-old feature called the "postage stamp" rate.
NOVA has said that the postage stamp stimulated natural gas development in remote regions of Alberta that would have been left undrilled with a distance-based transport tariff.
Palliser project manager Jeff Myers said in a statement that the line would provide new capacity for western Canadian producers "at a time of critical need."

Myers said Palliser would feed large increases in capacity planned for 1998 and afterward on TransCanada PipeLines Ltd's system and the Foothills/Northern Border network into U.S. and eastern Canadian markets.
